label: Brisnik: MISC1
title: Antidepressant use in a person with chronic heart failure and a first mild or moderate depressive episode
statement: Prescribed any antidepressant - and the patient has chronic heart failure and a first episode of mild or moderate depression

source.document: Brisnik V, et al. Deprescribing of antidepressants: indicators of high-risk and overprescribing. BMC Med 2024;22:193, Tables 3-4
source.citation: Brisnik V, Vukas J, Jung-Sievers C, et al. Deprescribing of antidepressants: development of indicators of high-risk and overprescribing using the RAND/UCLA Appropriateness Method. BMC Med 2024;22:193. doi:10.1186/s12916-024-03397-w

plain_summary: Review antidepressant use in a person with chronic heart failure and a first mild or moderate depressive episode. Consider why the medicine is used, its benefit for this person and the cardiac risks of the particular medicine.

medicine_groups.name: Antidepressants
medicine_groups.note: Listed brands can identify historical supplies. Current sale is not assumed. Dothiepin is another name for dosulepin and counts as the same medicine. Count bupropion only when the record identifies its use for the depressive episode under review. Exclude use for smoking cessation. Unknown purpose can support only a possible finding when the other criteria for review are met. Specialist intranasal esketamine is outside the antidepressant list used for this screen. Surmontil tablets and capsules contain trimipramine. Match trazodone by ingredient when no verified brand is available. Exclude doxepin cream used on the skin.

medicine_groups.name: Medicines that suggest chronic heart failure
medicine_groups.note: Use at least two different Group B medicines as supporting evidence for a possible finding when chronic heart failure is undocumented. Check that their courses plausibly overlap the antidepressant treatment under review. A course known to have ended beforehand cannot support this inference. Frusemide is the former Australian name for furosemide. Count both names as one medicine. When using two different Group B medicines as evidence of possible heart failure, require plausible treatment overlap with the antidepressant and exclude known separate courses. Use the supply date, quantity and stated daily use to work out the days covered by each course. If directions are unclear, ask how much was taken, how often and on which dates. The pharmacist judges borderline overlap. If neither the record nor the patient supports overlap, those supplies cannot support a possible finding. Sacubitril with valsartan, sacubitril + valsartan and Entresto are one medicine. Count them once, including across repeat supplies.

needs_facts.meets: A line recording chronic heart failure

needs_facts.what: First episode of mild or moderate depression
needs_facts.meets: The episode during the antidepressant course under review was the first and was mild or moderate. An earlier first episode does not qualify a later recurrence. A severe episode or no depressive episode during this course rules out the finding.

options.words: First depressive episode, mild or moderate
No depressive episode during this course

needs_facts.what: Reason for bupropion during this depressive episode
needs_facts.meets: Bupropion treated the depressive episode under review. Smoking cessation or another sole purpose excludes bupropion as the qualifying antidepressant. If its purpose is unknown, bupropion can support at most a possible finding.

options.words: For the depressive episode under review
Only for smoking cessation or another reason

needs_facts.what: Use of two different cardiac medicines during the antidepressant course
needs_facts.meets: Both different Group B medicines were used during the antidepressant course. This supports only a possible finding when chronic heart failure is undocumented. If fewer than two were used, the medicine clue is insufficient. An unknown answer leaves plausible but uncertain overlap unresolved. Neither answer establishes or rules out a diagnosis of heart failure.

options.words: Both cardiac medicines were used during the antidepressant course
Fewer than two were used during that course

rule_for_models: Require a Group A antidepressant supply under the Group A form and indication rules, and confirm a finding only by citing that supply and both fact lines for chronic heart failure and a first mild or moderate depressive episode. If chronic heart failure is ruled out or the episode is recurrent, severe or otherwise nonqualifying, report no finding. If either fact is missing or unspecified, report a possible finding naming each missing fact and citing the antidepressant, any qualifying fact and all supporting Group B supplies, but when heart failure is undocumented require two different Group B medicines whose overlap with the antidepressant is supported by the course dates, quantities and daily use or by patient clarification as described in Group B. Use a recorded reason for bupropion first. Ask about the reason for bupropion during this depressive episode only if its purpose is unclear and it could decide the finding. For undocumented heart failure, check dates, quantities and directions for two genuinely different Group B medicines. Ask about use of two different cardiac medicines during the antidepressant course only if their courses could overlap it and the dates do not settle this. Cite any clarification used. Confirmed overlap supports only a possible finding and leaves the diagnosis to be confirmed. If fewer than two overlap, the clue fails. An unknown answer keeps a plausible finding open.
cannot_be_seen: When not recorded: whether the heart failure is chronic, whether this is the first episode of depression, how severe it is, and whether talking therapy was tried. Medicines supplied by a hospital or another pharmacy.
ask_the_gp: Could you review whether the antidepressant is the best choice for this person, confirm any missing heart-failure or depression episode details, and consider non-drug treatment or an antidepressant review?
